zotero.abstractNote: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has become a cornerstone experimental technique in tissue biology, with gene expression data for over 100 million cells now available in public repositories. These methods learn denoised, low-dimensional representations of single-cell transcriptomes that can then be used for clustering, visualization, and downstream analysis. We organize the space of models to get scRNA-seq embeddings into factor models, autoencoders/VAEs, contrastive learning, and transformer-based foundation models, and discuss benchmarks and open problems.
